newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish lower in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish lower in quiet trading.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished lower in an afternoon of quiet trading, never shaking off pressure from strong data earlier.
Traders said a dealer selling weighed on the market heading into the close, with three firms seen as sellers.
Trading overall was light and rangebound.
"The only excitement was the surpising housing number," said Don Pullen, assistant vice president with Dean Witter Reynolds. "Everyone was looking for a decline and we found strength there," he said.

August single-family home sales rose 4.7 percent to an annual rate of 832,000 units, versus average trade estimates of 744,000. July new home sales were revised up to 795,000 units, from 783,000 units as originally reported.

A strong prices paid index in September's Chicago purchasing managers report also weighed on the market. September prices paid was 59.3 versus 51.8 in August. The overall business barometer fell to 56.3 from 60.0 in August.
"We went out holding the low and support at 109-3/32 but traders are now concerned about tomorrow's report," Pullen said. "We've got some big numbers to face."
The National Association of Purchasing Management report for September, to be released at 0900 CDT/1400 GMT on Tuesday, was forecast at 52.5 compared with 52.6 in the previous report.
On Friday, September U.S. payroll data will be released. Non-farm payrolls were seen up 166,000 compared with a 250,000 gain in August.
Traders said action was quiet after the early decline, with traders looking to sell rallies but unwilling to push the market through support at 109-00.
"I think that people have been long since part of last week and I don't think some of these guys got a chance to get out of stuff after these numbers this morning," a T-bond options trader said.
But while every uptick met with selling, the market was well-supported, he said.
"We saw some late pressure into the close but really, once we got the data we were pinned all afternoon into that narrow range," another T-bond futures trader said.
He said a December T-bond range of 108-16/32 to 110-10/32 could contain the market until Friday's critical jobs data.
"We started the week on a sour note, but we've got to get through more numbers," the trader said.
Dec bonds finished down 9/32 at 109-06/32, Dec Euros fell two bps at 94.21, March Euros were down three bps at 94.07 and March bills ended off three bps at 94.61.
